subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should the remaining work be limited to clearer dropped-media diagnostics, or should this issue also broaden/configure the host-local `MEDIA:` path policy?
rationale: Diagnostics are a bounded UX fix, but accepting more host-local paths changes the file-read and upload security boundary and overlaps the open configurable-root work.

options.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots Separately
options.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level and user-visible dropped-media reasons, while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable root expansion.

options.title: Canonicalize Root Policy Here
options.body: Use this issue to define the supported `MEDIA:` root policy, including any config or `tools.fs.roots` behavior.

options.title: Close As Current Policy
options.body: Treat the current file-read trust model and generic warning as enough, and require users to use managed roots or existing message-tool sends.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots Separately
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level and user-visible dropped-media reasons, while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable root expansion.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the current outbound media access policy points to this owner.
